results.one_row_per_submission: execute now takes the caller's row — execute(request, workflow=None, user_id=None). Both submit paths create the row with _get_user_id(request) and pass it in; _run_workflow_bg loads that row and hands it back, so the id POST /api/workflows returns is the id the run writes. execute(request) still works for callers that pass none and creates the row with the user_id when one is known. Test (a) proves it through the real routes and its break is quoted: '_run_workflow_bg' calling execute(workflow.request) fails with "assert 'pending' == 'completed'" — the pre-fix behaviour.
results.progress_as_it_happens: The row is committed before the run starts. Each node's phase record and the row's visible status are written in a transaction of its own, from a chain of tasks the synchronous on_phase callback schedules (one writer at a time, in node order). _NODE_STATUS is read: triage→TRIAGE, plan/feasibility→PLAN, implement/domain_review→IMPLEMENT, validate→VALIDATE, review→REVIEW; nodes outside the map (context, regrounding, checks, build_loop, escalation) leave the status where it is. The end-of-run flush writes nothing twice: a written flag per save, and a retried write never moves a terminal row. Test (c) proves the mid-run visibility from a second connection and its break is quoted: flushing instead of committing fails with "the run had already ended (completed) when the phase was first seen".
results.terminal_cast_cannot_lose_a_result: WorkflowStatus(state.status) moved inside the guarded region. An unknown terminal ends the row BLOCKED with the raw terminal in error, committed. Test (d) drives it end to end: a tmp workflow whose loop exhausts into on_exhausted_status 'frobnicate' — which spec.parse does not check against TERMINAL_STATUSES (spec.py:381-384 check only mutual exclusion with on_exhausted), so it reaches state.end unvalidated (executor.py:951) and the cast as a non-member. Its break is quoted: narrowing the guard to OSError lets 'ValueError: \'frobnicate\' is not a valid WorkflowStatus' escape the request, exactly the pre-fix loss.
results.tests_a_to_d: tests/test_api.py: TestOneRowPerSubmission, TestSubmissionsBelongToTheirCaller (auth configured via jwt_secret; both paths keep the caller's user_id; the caller can list and read), TestProgressIsVisibleMidRun, TestAnUnknownTerminalKeepsTheResult. All through httpx ASGITransport against the real routes, real engine, real graph and the existing provider-free double, which still bills.
